metadata.name: read
metadata.label: read
metadata.description: Read a file. Reads text files, plus images in jpg, png, gif or webp format that come back as attachments. Text output is cut at 2000 lines or 50KB, whichever limit is reached first. For large files, page through with offset and limit. When you need the whole file, keep continuing with offset until it is complete.
promptGuidelines: Inspect files with read, not cat or sed.

path.description: File to read, as a relative or absolute path

offset.description: First line to read, counting from 1

limit.description: Upper bound on the lines returned

metadata.name: bash
metadata.label: bash
metadata.description: Run a bash command; it starts in the current working directory. The result carries stdout and stderr, and output keeps only the last 2000 lines or 50KB, whichever limit is reached first. When output is cut, the full output is saved to a temporary file. Accepts an optional timeout in seconds.
metadata.promptSnippet: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

metadata.name: edit
metadata.label: edit
metadata.description: Edit one file by replacing exact text. Each edits[].oldText must match exactly one region of the original file, and no two regions may overlap. Changes within one block or on adjacent lines belong in a single edit, not in overlapping edits. Never pad an edit with large unchanged regions just to join distant changes.
metadata.promptSnippet: Replace exact text in a file, including several disjoint edits in one call
promptGuidelines: Edit suits precise changes, and every edits[].oldText has to match the file exactly
To change several separate places in one file, make a single edit call with one edits[] entry per place rather than several edit calls
Each edits[].oldText is looked up in the original file, not in what earlier edits leave behind. Never emit overlapping or nested edits; fold nearby changes into one edit.
Make edits[].oldText as short as it can be while still occurring once in the file. Never pad it with large unchanged regions.

path.description: File to edit, as a relative or absolute path

oldText.description: Exact text that one targeted edit replaces. It must occur once in the original file and must not overlap any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Text that takes the place of oldText in this edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Every edit is located in the original file, never in the output of an earlier edit. Overlapping or nested edits are rejected. Changes within one block or on adjacent lines go into a single edit.

metadata.name: grep
metadata.label: grep
metadata.description: Find a pattern in file contents. Returns each matching line with its file path and line number. Honors .gitignore. Output stops at 100 matches or 50KB, whichever limit is reached first. Lines longer than 500 chars are cut.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

metadata.label: ls
metadata.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)
